name: Non-syndromic Unicoronal and Sagittal Craniosynostosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Craniosynostosis

criteria.description: Premature fusion of the unicoronal and/or sagittal cranial sutures confirmed by imaging
Characteristic skull shape abnormalities such as anterior plagiocephaly (unicoronal) or scaphocephaly (sagittal)
Lack of associated syndromic features such as limb anomalies or genetic syndromes
Normal neurodevelopmental milestones without evidence of cognitive impairment at diagnosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of premature fusion of unicoronal and/or sagittal sutures with characteristic cranial deformity and absence of syndromic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing may be used to exclude syndromic causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Anterior Plagiocephaly due to Unicoronal Suture Fusion
searchTerms: uneven forehead shape from fused skull suture
asymmetric head shape due to coronal suture fusion

pathognomonic.symptomName: Scaphocephaly due to Sagittal Suture Fusion
searchTerms: sagittal suture fusion causing elongated head

pathognomonic.symptomName: Palpable Ridging along Fused Cranial Sutures
searchTerms: bump felt along fused skull joints
ridge on skull where sutures closed early
raised eyebrow bone on one side

occasional.symptomName: Increased Intracranial Pressure Signs (e.g., irritability, vomiting)
searchTerms: vomiting and irritability from brain swelling

rare.symptomName: Visual Impairment due to Optic Nerve Compression
searchTerms: vision problems from optic nerve pressure
eye nerve compression causing vision loss

imaging: CT scan showing premature fusion of unicoronal and/or sagittal sutures
3D cranial reconstruction demonstrating skull shape abnormalities
genetic: Absence of mutations in syndromic craniosynostosis genes (e.g., FGFR2, TWIST1) in non-syndromic cases
other: Physical examination revealing palpable suture ridging and characteristic cranial deformities

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of limb anomalies or other systemic features
Known pathogenic mutations in FGFR or TWIST genes
Multiple suture involvement with syndromic phenotype
Absence of suture fusion on imaging
Improvement with repositioning and physical therapy

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure (e.g., vomiting, irritability)
Visual disturbances or optic nerve dysfunction
references: Cohen MM Jr. Craniosynostosis: Diagnosis, Evaluation, and Management. 3rd ed. Oxford University Press; 2000.
Wilkie AO, Morriss-Kay GM. Genetics of craniosynostosis. Curr Opin Pediatr. 2001;13(6):610-616.
